10.1016_j.cej.2026.174739: Transition metal (oxy)carbides are promising electrode materials in protonic ceramic cells (PCCs) for operation in hydrocarbon atmospheres due to their structural stability under these conditions, which addresses a known issue in Ni-based cermets, and their satisfactory electrical properties. In this work, several (oxy)carbides — Mo 2 C x O y , ZrC x O y , WC x O y , and NbC x O y — are evaluated, all exhibiting phase stability in methane. The chemical compatibility of the materials with the BaCe 0.9 Y 0.1 O 3- δ (BCY) electrolyte is also examined, revealing that only the molybdenum-based composition does not form secondary phases. The application of the molybdenum (oxy)carbide in biogas is constrained by its susceptibility to oxidation in CO 2 , with thermodynamic and kinetic studies indicating resistance to oxidation only at low temperatures, where the reforming process is limited. Notably, the Mo 2 C x O y -BCY composite electrode shows considerable improvement after one week in pure (humidified) CH 4 at 800 °C, with polarisation resistance decreasing by ~82%, highlighting the beneficial effect of prolonged exposure to the hydrocarbon atmosphere. Elemental analysis and thermogravimetric measurements suggest an increased C/O ratio after methane treatment, as also confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and corroborated by a slight expansion of the crystal lattice observed by X-ray diffractometry (XRD), contributing to the electrical and catalytic properties. A stable open-circuit voltage (OCV) of ~0.8 V at 800 °C for one week demonstrates that the anode is not degraded in CH 4 . However, a decrease to ~0.5 V at 700 °C indicates a limitation in low-temperature internal reforming. Finally, variation of hydrogen partial pressure further reveals that the electrode, with a p H 2 − 0.37 dependence, is rate-limited by hydrogen adsorption/desorption and surface diffusion kinetics, which should occur on the (oxy)carbide surface. • Mo 2 C x O y is chemically compatible with yttria-doped barium cerate, while ZrC x O y and NbC x O y are not. • CO 2 exposure drives oxidation of (oxy)carbides, which limits their applicability in biogas. • The anionic sublattice of Mo (oxy)carbide is recarburised in methane. • Long-term CH 4 operation enhances electrochemical activity by ~82%. • The electrochemical mechanism of the electrode is outlined.
10.1016_j.ijmultiphaseflow.2026.105738: 3D direct numerical simulation of electrolysis is applied to investigate the growth and detachment of bubbles at electrodes. The moving gas-liquid interface is modeled employing the VOF-based method. To ensure the accuracy of the simulations, a mesh-independence study has been performed. The simulations include the growth phase of the bubbles followed by their detachment from the electrode surface and the results are validated with analytical models and experimental data. The bubble growth is diffusion controlled leading to the scaling R=2βt1/2, but the growth exponent is overpredicted by our simulation during initial stage. Furthermore, it is proved that the nucleation sites of the bubble strongly influence gas transport by measuring the relevant Sherwood number. Finally, we investigate the effects of contact angle and nucleation sites on bubble detachment behavior, and compare the detachment radius with Fritz's formula, the results show a good agreement, confirming that buoyancy is the dominant driving force. As the nucleation sites increase, the induced bubble coalescence accelerates the bubble detachment. Taken together, these findings give us valuable insights into improving gas bubble removal and enhancing overall electrolysis efficiency.
10.1021_jacs.5c20558: Disulfides are pivotal chemical motifs in life science, biomedicine, and materials science; nevertheless, their efficient construction arouses tremendous challenges due to inherent fragility to redox environments. Herein, we disclosed an electroreductive disulfuration protocol, leveraging readily accessible electrophiles to achieve divergent coupling via the tetrasulfide radical anion [ t BuSSSS t Bu] •– with tunable radical and ionic routes, respectively. The distinct reductive potential of the electrophilic partners relative to the tetrasulfide reduction potential ( t BuSSSS t Bu, E p = −1.08 V vs Ag/AgCl) served as the electrochemical switch. The dissociation of the [ t BuSSSS t Bu] •– generated from single-electron reduction regulated the reaction pathway toward radical (favored by higher potential electrophiles, E p = −0.8 to −1.5 V vs Ag/AgCl) and ionic (favored by lower potential electrophiles, E p = −2.0 to −3.0 V vs Ag/AgCl) pathways. This protocol afforded straightforward access to unsymmetric disulfides with diversely functional pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and natural product scaffolds. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidated the crucial role of the central S–S bond lability from tetrasulfide for two distinct mechanistic pathways. Gram-scaled continuous flow synthesis showcased the operational robustness and scalability of this protocol. The potent antibacterial activity observed against Staphylococcus aureus underscored its great potential for accelerating the discovery of disulfide-based therapeutic agents.
